text:
Jason Robertson has spent the last week reading about himself in trade rumors, from an insider's floated swap for Nikita Kucherov to analysts doubting he signs long-term in Dallas. On Sunday he gave the Stars a reason to hold on, finishing a Roope Hintz feed on the backhand 2:56 into overtime for a 2-1 win over Florida.

It was a tight, grinding game between two teams that know what playoff hockey feels like. Florida, still without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, had the better first period, and Dallas managed a remarkable 0.06 expected goals (the quality of chances) in those 20 minutes. The Panthers had 50 shot attempts to 40 overall. But Dallas created more of the dangerous stuff, 2.59 expected goals to 1.87, and deserved the win in 64% of our replays, mostly because of what happened at even strength and in overtime.

Matthew Tkachuk opened it on a power play 4:27 into the second, a snap shot from Sam Reinhart and Seth Jones that was his 700th career point, a day after the Tkachuk family's night in St. Louis. Wyatt Johnston tied it under five minutes later from Thomas Harley and Robertson, and then the goalies took over. Jamie Benn, a night removed from his 1,000th point, had the best chance that didn't go in, a 26% look in the second that Akira Schmid stopped. Schmid's best save came in overtime on Mikko Rantanen, and it bought Florida about a minute.

Casey DeSmith, first star, made 25 saves on 26 shots, about 0.9 goals better than expected, and Schmid was 0.6 better at the other end. Harley played 30:54 with Miro Heiskanen still out, and Dallas outchanced Florida 0.68 to 0.17 in the overtime itself.

Florida's three-game win streak ends with a point, which it will take. For Dallas, it's a second straight win after the 8-3 loss in Winnipeg on Thursday, and another night where Robertson looked like the player nobody should want to move.
headline: Robertson's overtime backhand sinks the Panthers
